topics.label: Introduction to the initiation and resolution of inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer opens the session by welcoming the class and framing how the lecture synthesises previously introduced immune components.

topics.label: Innate recognition principles of PAMPs, DAMPs, and pattern recognition receptors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular criteria and receptor characteristics that allow the innate immune system to detect microbes and tissue damage while discriminating self from non-self.

topics.label: Pattern recognition receptor classes and inflammasome signalling pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the specific families of pattern recognition receptors, their downstream intracellular signalling mechanisms, and the assembly of inflammasomes for cytokine processing.

topics.label: Inflammatory cascade, leukocyte recruitment, and systemic outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the physiological chain of events following immune activation, covering sentinel mediator release, leukocyte recruitment, lymphatic drainage, and systemic complications such as septic shock.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic pathology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the active and passive mechanisms that terminate inflammation, the tissue repair process, and the outcomes of unresolved inflammation including chronic disease and granulomas.

topics.label: Lecture close and next topic preview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture and announces the topic of the following session.
